applies_to: Yaskawa HV600 Narrow and Enclosed Bypass packages (H6B models) connected to BACnet MS/TP at the bypass controller.
summary: On the HV600 bypass the BACnet MS/TP connection is made at the bypass control board (terminal TB3), which exposes drive and bypass data from one address. The list has the HV600 drive objects plus bypass analog and digital I/O, bypass run/transfer and emergency-override commands, HOA and contactor status, bypass fault flags and drive/bypass fault codes.
firmware: PICS lists application software VST8004xx, firmware revision 2.01; the manual covers bypass firmware up to 00450/00451
notes: Objects named Not Used (AI3, AI5, AV34, BV1, BV2, BV5, BV6, BV66-BV68, BV100) are left out.
Most objects have a long name and a shorter network display name; the long name is listed and the display name is given as 'Shown as' in the description.
AV1 drives the drive only; the manual says to command the bypass with BV58-BV71 instead.
AV4 must not be combined with BO1-BO3 or BV12; AV5 must not be combined with AV1, BO4 or BV9-BV11.
BO8-BO11 only work when the matching Z2-xx output function is set to 99 (Not Used).
Each description gives the Modbus register where the manual lists one (hex).

source.title: YASKAWA HV600 Narrow & Enclosed Bypass Technical Reference (section 10.3, BACnet Communications)

integration.summary: Wire BACnet MS/TP to TB3 on the bypass board and set H5-08 = 3 (BACnet), H5-01 address, H5-02 baud and the device instance in H5-14/H5-15, then cycle power or set H5-20 = 1. Set b1-01 = 2 and b1-02 = 2 or 8 so the network supplies the speed reference and run command, then write BV58 and AV2. Read BV89, BV90 and AV42.

minimum_points.name: Bypass AUTO Mode Status
minimum_points.why: HOA in AUTO, so BMS commands apply

integration.enable: b1-01 Frequency Reference Selection 1 = 2 (Serial Communications) and b1-02 Run Command Selection 1 = 2 (Serial Communications) or 8 (AUTO Command + Serial Run). Defaults are b1-01 = 1 (analog input) and b1-02 = 7 (AUTO Command + Term Run). Command the bypass with BV58-BV71, not AV1. Monitoring, parameter access and fault reset work whatever b1-01/b1-02 are set to.
integration.heartbeat: H5-05 = 1 (default) turns on CE detection: if nothing is received for H5-09 (0.0-10.0 s, default 2.0 s) the unit acts per H5-04: 0 ramp to stop, 1 coast, 2 fast stop (C1-09), 3 alarm only and keep running (default), 4 run at the H5-34 speed.
integration.remote_sensors: AV3 PI Setpoint Cmd lets the BMS write the PI setpoint (0-100 %); BO4 Ref Sel:PI Setpoint selects it. BV72-BV79 act as network copies of the bypass digital inputs.
setup: H5-08 = 3 selects BACnet; H5-01 is the MS/TP address (BACnet range 0-7F, default 1FH) and must be unique.
H5-02 baud for BACnet: setting 3 (9600, default), 4 (19200), 5 (38400) or 7 (76800 bps).
Device instance = H5-14 (low word) + H5-15 (high word), in hex; default 1.
Communication settings take effect after a power cycle or H5-20 = 1.
DIP switch S1 on the bypass board enables termination; turn it on only at the ends of the line.
Up to 127 bypasses per MS/TP segment; device object name and location (40 characters each) are writable over BACnet MS/TP.
gotchas: H5-04 defaults to Alarm Only, so the unit keeps running when BACnet traffic stops.
AV1 only commands the drive; use BV58-BV71 for the bypass.
BV56 Parameter Enter writes EEPROM; don't use it cyclically.
BO8-BO11 do nothing unless the matching Z2-xx output is set to 99.
Frequency objects use the o1-03 display units.
